title: feat(claim): add activation-nonce check to Claim verification
body:
## Background

Part of the roadmap #1480 (sticky forced-handoff / concurrent-claim
cross-session collision gap). Today, `idd-claim.instructions.md`'s
`## Claim verification` section and `idd-overview-core.instructions.md`'s
Claim revalidation gate key ownership purely on `agent-id`/`claim-id`
token-string equality. Nothing is posted at forced-handoff
adopt-verbatim time ("no separate `claimed-by supersedes: none` post is
required for the transfer itself"), so two independent sessions
adopting the identical sticky successor pair both see byte-identical
GitHub state and both pass every existing check identically -- a
verified near-miss (see #1480's background).

**Interaction with #1439 (orchestrator delegation exception).** #1439
defines a legitimate case where a second session (a delegated worker)
intentionally activates using an already-claimed `claim-id` it never
posted itself -- structurally the same "second session, same
`claim-id`" shape this nonce check is built to catch. #1439 is
`Blocked by` this issue precisely so its delegation path can be
defined as a third, nonce-aware activation path once this nonce
mechanism exists, rather than the two of them being designed blind to
each other. Keep the nonce-posting and nonce-comparison logic added
here extensible to a third activation path (not hardcoded to only
"ordinary" and "forced-handoff adopt-verbatim"), so #1439 does not
need to reopen this issue's design to add it.

## Proposed change

- In `idd-claim.instructions.md`'s `## Claim verification` section,
  immediately after the existing adopt-verbatim text, add: at claim
  activation time -- both an ordinary fresh `claimed-by supersedes:
  none` post and a forced-handoff adopt-verbatim reconciliation -- post
  a lightweight trusted marker comment carrying a fresh session-local
  nonce alongside the `claim-id`.
- At the Claim revalidation gate in
  `idd-overview-core.instructions.md`, check the locally-held nonce
  against the latest posted nonce for the active `claim-id`, alongside
  the existing `claim-id` match. A detected second activation with a
  different nonce routes through the existing same-second /
  later-competing-claim tie-break logic
  (`idd-claim.instructions.md`'s Claim verification steps), rather than
  proceeding as sole owner.
- Backward compatibility: an active claim whose most recent relevant
  marker predates this change (no nonce field at all) must not be
  treated as a detected collision -- absence of a nonce is "no
  comparison possible," not "mismatch."
- Update `idd-claim.instructions.md`'s Claim-state parsing rules if a
  new marker field requires it, and add unit/integration test coverage
  for: same-nonce (no collision), different-nonce (collision detected,
  routes to tie-break), and missing-nonce (backward-compatible pass).
- Regenerate mirrors with `node scripts/sync-docs.mjs --apply` and
  confirm `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` reports zero drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Claim activation (ordinary fresh claim and forced-handoff
      adopt-verbatim) posts a fresh session-local activation nonce.
- [ ] The Claim revalidation gate detects a second activation with a
      mismatched nonce for the same `claim-id` and routes it through
      the existing tie-break logic instead of silently proceeding.
- [ ] A pre-existing marker with no nonce field is not treated as a
      collision (backward compatibility preserved).
- [ ] New tests cover same-nonce, different-nonce, and missing-nonce
      cases.
- [ ] The nonce-posting/comparison design does not hardcode exactly
      two activation paths -- a future third path (#1439's delegation
      exception) can register a legitimate activation without
      reopening this issue's design.
- [ ] `node scripts/audit-docs.mjs --check` reports zero drift.

Part of roadmap #1480.
